title.zh: 卷一百十六 國語解
title.raw: 卷一百十六 國語解 Volume 116: Explanation of State Language

sentences.zh: 史自遷、固，以迄晉、唐，其為書雄深浩博，讀者未能盡曉。

translations.literal: Histories from Sima Qian and Ban Gu down through the Jin and Tang — their books are grand, deep, vast, and abstruse; readers cannot fully comprehend them.
translations.idiomatic: From Sima Qian and Ban Gu through the Jin and Tang dynasties, the histories they wrote are vast and profound — so much so that readers cannot fully grasp them on their own.

sentences.zh: 於是裴 、顏師古、李賢、何超、董沖諸儒，訓詁音釋，然後制度、名物、方言、奇字，可以一覽而周知。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pei Yin, Yan Shigu, Li Xian, He Chao, Dong Chong, and other scholars provided exegetical and phonetic glosses, so that institutions, objects, dialect terms, and unusual characters could be surveyed at a glance and fully understood.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars such as Pei Yin, Yan Shigu, Li Xian, He Chao, and Dong Chong then supplied phonetic and exegetical notes, making it possible to survey institutions, material objects, regional speech, and obscure characters in a single reading and understand them completely.

translations.literal: Their help to later students is great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: They have been of immense benefit to later generations of scholars.

sentences.zh: 遼之初興，與奚、室韋密邇，土俗言語大概近俚。

translations.literal: When Liao first arose, it was close to the Xi and Shiwei; local custom and speech were generally near to the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao state first emerged, it lay close to the Xi and Shiwei peoples, and its local customs and language were largely rustic and colloquial.

sentences.zh: 至太祖、太宗，奄有朔方，其治雖三用漢法，而先世奇首、遙輦之制尚多存者。

translations.literal: By the Taizu and Taizong Emperors, they covered the northern regions; though their governance thrice employed Han law, many institutions of earlier generations — the Qishou and Yaolian systems — still remained.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Emperor Taizu and Emperor Taizong, the Liao had seized the northern frontier. Although their administration repeatedly adopted Chinese law, many institutions of the earlier Qishou and Yaolian eras still survived.

sentences.zh: 子孫相繼，亦遵守而不易。

translations.literal: Successive descendants also preserved them without change.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants preserved these customs in succession, altering nothing.

sentences.zh: 故史之所載，官制、宮衛、部族、地理，率以國語為之稱號。

translations.literal: Therefore what the history records — official institutions, palace guards, tribal divisions, and geography — generally uses the state language for its designations.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the offices, palace guards, tribal divisions, and place names recorded in the history are for the most part designated in the Khitan state language.

sentences.zh: 不有注釋以辨之，則世何從而知，後何從而考哉。

translations.literal: Without annotations to distinguish them, how would the age know, and how would posterity investigate?
translations.idiomatic: Without explanatory glosses to clarify them, how could the present age understand them, or later generations verify them?

sentences.zh: 今即本史三互研究，撰次遼國語解以附其後，庶幾讀者無齟齬之患云。

translations.literal: Now, taking this history's three sections for mutual study, we compile and arrange an Explanation of the Liao State Language to append after it, so that readers may be free from the trouble of discord.
translations.idiomatic: We have therefore cross-referenced the three sections of this history and compiled an Explanation of the Liao State Language to append here, so that readers need not stumble over unfamiliar terms.

translations.literal: Annals of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Emperor Taizu

sentences.zh: 耶律氏、蕭氏 本紀首書太祖姓耶律氏，繼書皇后蕭氏，則有國之初，已分二姓矣。

translations.literal: Yelü Clan, Xiao Clan — the basic annals first record Taizu surnamed Yelü, then record the empress surnamed Xiao; thus from the founding of the state, two surnames were already divided.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü and Xiao: the annals open by giving Taizu's surname as Yelü and the empress's as Xiao — showing that two clans were distinguished from the very founding of the state.

sentences.zh: 有謂始興之地曰世裏，譯者以世裏為耶律，故國族皆以耶律為姓。

translations.literal: Some say the place of initial rise was called Shili; translators took Shili as Yelü, so the state clan all took Yelü as surname.
translations.idiomatic: One account holds that the land where the dynasty arose was called Shili; translators rendered this as Yelü, and the imperial clan accordingly adopted Yelü as its surname.

sentences.zh: 有謂述律皇后兄子名蕭翰者，為宣武軍節度使，其妹複為皇后，故後族皆以蕭為姓。

translations.literal: Some say Empress Shulü's elder brother's son, named Xiao Han, was Military Commissioner of Xuanwu Army; his younger sister again became empress, so the consort clan all took Xiao as surname.
translations.idiomatic: Another account says that Xiao Han, nephew of Empress Shulü and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, had a sister who also became empress; the consort clan therefore took the surname Xiao.

sentences.zh: 其說與紀不合，故陳大任不取。

translations.literal: These explanations do not accord with the annals, so Chen Daren did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: These explanations conflict with the annals, and Chen Daren rejected them.

sentences.zh: 又有言以漢字書者曰耶律、蕭，以契丹字書者曰移剌、石抹，則亦無可考矣。

translations.literal: There is also a saying that written in Han characters they are Yelü and Xiao, written in Khitan script they are Yila and Shimo — but this too cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Some also say that in Chinese characters the names appear as Yelü and Xiao, while in Khitan script they appear as Yila and Shimo — but this too cannot be substantiated.

translations.literal: Xialaiyi Shilie — a district name.
translations.idiomatic: Xialaiyi Shilie: the name of a district.

sentences.zh: 諸宮下皆有石烈，設官治之。

translations.literal: Under each palace there are shilie; officials are established to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace district had its shilie subdivisions, each overseen by appointed officials.

translations.literal: Mili — a smaller subdivision of a district.
translations.idiomatic: Mili: a sub-district, smaller than a full district.

sentences.zh: 撻馬 沙裏 撻馬，人從也。

translations.literal: Tama, Shali — tama means personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Tama and Shali: tama means personal attendants.

translations.literal: Shali means young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shali denotes a young nobleman or attendant lord.

translations.literal: An office that supervises and leads the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: An official charged with supervising the people.

translations.literal: Later there were those called only tama.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title was shortened to tama alone.

sentences.zh: 大迭烈府 即迭剌部之府也。

translations.literal: Great Dielie Prefecture — that is, the prefecture of the Diela tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Great Dielie Prefecture: the administrative seat of the Diela tribe.

sentences.zh: 初，阻午可汗與其弟撒裏本領之，及太祖以部夷離 即位，因強大難制，析為二院。

translations.literal: At first, Khan Zuwu and his younger brother Saben jointly led it; when Taizu acceded as tribal yilij, because it was strong and hard to control, it was divided into two courts.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Khan Zuwu and his brother Saben jointly governed it. When Taizu acceded as tribal yilij, the tribe had grown so powerful that it was split into two courts.

translations.literal: Lie and la sound close to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The characters lie and la are phonetically similar.

translations.literal: Yili — a great office commanding armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yili: a high office with command over armies and cavalry.

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huitong era, it was changed to Great King.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huitong era, the title was changed to Great King.

translations.literal: Jihui Guo — two pronunciations, wo and tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Jihui Guo: a place name with two pronunciations, wo and tuo.

translations.literal: A place name.
translations.idiomatic: A place name.

sentences.zh: 阿主沙裏 阿主，父祖稱。

translations.literal: Azhu Shali — azhu is a title for father and grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu Shali: azhu is an honorific for one's father or grandfather.

translations.literal: Tiyin — an office managing clan relations.
translations.idiomatic: Tiyin: an official in charge of clan affairs.

translations.literal: That is, the duty of the Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Equivalent to the Chinese office of Director of the Imperial Clan.

translations.literal: Xi — the lower character is pronounced xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi: the second character is pronounced xi.

translations.literal: A state name.
translations.idiomatic: The name of a state.

translations.literal: The territory of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Land belonging to the Central Capital.

translations.literal: Heichezi — a state.
translations.idiomatic: Heichezi: a tribal state.

translations.literal: Named for skill in making carts and tents.
translations.idiomatic: So named because its people were skilled at making carts and tents.

sentences.zh: 契丹之先，嘗遣人往學之。

translations.literal: The Khitan forebears once sent people to go and learn from them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ancestors once sent envoys to learn these crafts from them.

translations.literal: Yuyue — a noble office with no specific duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyue: a high honorific office with no defined administrative function.

sentences.zh: 其位居北、南大王上，非有大功德者不授。

translations.literal: Its rank stands above the Northern and Southern Great Kings; it is not conferred except on those of great merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Its rank exceeded that of the Northern and Southern Great Kings, and was granted only to men of exceptional merit.

translations.literal: Eagle Army — eagle is a fierce bird;
translations.idiomatic: Eagle Army: the eagle is a fierce bird of prey;

translations.literal: using it to name the army takes the meaning of swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: naming an army after it conveys the idea of speed and agility.

sentences.zh: 後記龍軍、虎軍、鐵鷂軍者，仿此。

translations.literal: Later records of Dragon Army, Tiger Army, and Iron Harrier Army follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Later references to the Dragon Army, Tiger Army, and Iron Harrier Army follow the same principle.

translations.literal: <One>
translations.idiomatic: <Note 1>

translations.literal: Nianggai — the upper character is pronounced wan.
translations.idiomatic: Nianggai: the first character is pronounced wan.

translations.literal: A place name.
translations.idiomatic: A place name.

sentences.zh: 西樓 遼有四樓：在上京者曰西樓；

translations.literal: Western Tower — Liao had four towers: at the Supreme Capital was called Western Tower;
translations.idiomatic: Western Tower: the Liao had four towers; the one at the Supreme Capital was the Western Tower;

translations.literal: Mount Muye was called Southern Tower;
translations.idiomatic: Mount Muye was the Southern Tower;

translations.literal: Longhua Prefecture was called Eastern Tower;
translations.idiomatic: Longhua Prefecture was the Eastern Tower;

translations.literal: Tang Prefecture was called Northern Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Prefecture was the Northern Tower.

translations.literal: Seasonal hunting excursions were always conducted among the four towers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperors hunted seasonally, moving among the four towers.

sentences.zh: 阿點夷離的 阿點，貴稱。

translations.literal: Adian Yilide — adian is an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Adian Yilide: adian is an honorific form of address.

translations.literal: Yilide is the title for a great minister's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yilide denotes the wife of a high minister.

translations.literal: Jiuxia — jiu is an army name.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxia: jiu is the name of a military unit.

translations.literal: Xia means the sense of control and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xia conveys the meaning of command and restraint.

sentences.zh: 夷離畢 即三知政事，後置夷離畢院以掌刑政。

translations.literal: Yilibi — that is, one of the Three Directors of Affairs; later the Yilibi Court was established to manage criminal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yilibi: equivalent to one of the Three Directors of Affairs; later a Yilibi Court was created to oversee criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 宋刁約使遼有詩雲「押宴夷離畢」，知其為執政官也。

translations.literal: Song envoy Diao Yue, on mission to Liao, had a poem saying 'presiding over the banquet, Yilibi' — knowing thereby that it was a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoy Diao Yue wrote in a poem on his mission to Liao, 'presiding at the banquet, the Yilibi' — showing that this was a chief ministerial office.

sentences.zh: 射鬼箭 凡帝親征，服介胄，祭諸先帝，出則取死囚一人，置所向之方，亂矢射之，名射鬼箭，以祓不祥。

translations.literal: Shooting Ghost Arrows — whenever the emperor personally campaigned, wearing armor, he sacrificed to the former emperors; upon departure he took one condemned prisoner, placed him in the direction of advance, and shot him with a volley of arrows — called Shooting Ghost Arrows, to expel ill omens.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting Ghost Arrows: when the emperor led a campaign in person, clad in armor, he first sacrificed to his ancestors. On departure he took a condemned prisoner, placed him in the direction of march, and riddled him with arrows — a rite called Shooting Ghost Arrows, intended to ward off misfortune.

translations.literal: Upon returning the army, they then shot captives.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, captives were shot instead.

translations.literal: Later it came to serve as an instrument of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Later the practice was incorporated into penal law.

translations.literal: Baoli — the name of a wicked man.
translations.idiomatic: Baoli: the name of a villain.

sentences.zh: 大、小鵠軍 二室韋軍號也。

translations.literal: Great and Small Goose Armies — two Shiwei army designations.
translations.idiomatic: Great and Small Goose Armies: designations of two Shiwei military units.

translations.literal: Shen — what attendants carry.
translations.idiomatic: Shen: a standard carried by attendants.

sentences.zh: 以旄牛尾為之，纓槍屬也。

translations.literal: Made of yak-tail, belonging to the tassel-spear category.
translations.idiomatic: Made from yak tails, it belongs to the category of tasseled spears.

sentences.zh: 龍眉宮 太祖取天梯、蒙國、別魯三山之勢於葦澱，射金齪箭以識之，名龍眉宮。

translations.literal: Dragon Eyebrow Palace — Taizu took the terrain formed by the three mountains Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu at the reed marsh, shot a golden cuo arrow to mark it, and named it Dragon Eyebrow Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Eyebrow Palace: Taizu selected a site at a reed marsh where three mountains — Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu — converged, marked it by shooting a golden cuo arrow, and named it Dragon Eyebrow Palace.

sentences.zh: 神冊三年，築都城於其地，臨潢府是也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Sence, a capital city was built on that site — this is Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Sence era, a capital was built there — present-day Linhuang Prefecture.

translations.literal: Cuo — ce angle cut; the name of an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Cuo, pronounced with the ce initial and jiao final: the name of an arrow type.

translations.literal: Xiaoli — a Shiwei tribal division name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoli: the name of a Shiwei tribe.

sentences.zh: 君基太一神 福神名。

translations.literal: Lord Foundation Great Unity Spirit — the name of a fortune deity.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Foundation Great Unity Spirit: the name of a god of good fortune.

sentences.zh: 其神所臨之國，君能建極，孚於上下，則治化升平，民享多福。

translations.literal: In the state where this spirit presides, if the ruler can establish the ultimate standard and win trust above and below, then governance and transformation ascend to peace and the people enjoy abundant fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In the land over which this deity presides, if the ruler upholds the highest standards and earns the trust of high and low alike, the realm enjoys peace and the people receive abundant blessings.

translations.literal: Talin — an office name.
translations.idiomatic: Talin: an official title.

sentences.zh: 後二室韋部改為僕射，又名司空。

translations.literal: Later the two Shiwei divisions were changed to Vice Director, also called Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later the two Shiwei divisions were retitled Vice Director, also known as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 舍利 契丹豪民耍裹頭巾者，納牛駝十頭，馬百疋，乃給官名曰舍利。

translations.literal: Sheli — Khitan magnates who sported wrapped headcloths, upon paying ten oxen and camels and a hundred horses, were granted an office called sheli.
translations.idiomatic: Sheli: wealthy Khitan men who wore wrapped headcloths could purchase the title by contributing ten oxen or camels and a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 後遂為諸帳官，以郎君系之。

translations.literal: Later it became an office of the various tents, linked with the title of young lord.
translations.idiomatic: It later became a tent-office title, paired with the rank of young lord.

translations.literal: Aluduo Li — also called Aludun.
translations.idiomatic: Aluduo Li, also known as Aludun.

translations.literal: A noble and eminent name.
translations.idiomatic: An honorific of high distinction.

sentences.zh: 遼於越官兼此者，惟曷魯耳。

translations.literal: Among Liao yuyue officials who also held this, only Helu.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Liao yuyue officials who also held this title, only Helu did so.

translations.literal: Xuandi — chief prison official.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi: the chief prison administrator.

translations.literal: Changgun — an office name.
translations.idiomatic: Changgun: an official title.

translations.literal: In charge of Yaolian tribal household registers and related matters;
translations.idiomatic: Responsible for Yaolian tribal household registers and related affairs;

sentences.zh: 奚六部常袞掌奚之族屬。

translations.literal: the Changgun of the Six Xi Divisions managed Xi clan relations.
translations.idiomatic: the Changgun of the Six Xi Divisions oversaw Xi clan affairs.

translations.literal: Maohai — a state ruler's name.
translations.idiomatic: Maohai: the name of a foreign ruler.

translations.literal: Ke Shilu — ke is an office name.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shilu: ke is an official title.

translations.literal: Shilu is a personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu is a person's name.

translations.literal: Later Ke Lang and Ke Taishen follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Later titles such as Ke Lang and Ke Taishen follow the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 烏魯古、阿裏只 太祖及述律後受 降時所乘二馬名也，因賜 夫婦以為名。

translations.literal: Ulugu, Alizhi — the names of two horses ridden when Taizu and Empress Shulü received surrender; the couple were granted these as names.
translations.idiomatic: Ulugu and Alizhi: names of two horses ridden by Taizu and Empress Shulü when accepting a surrender; the names were bestowed on the couple.

translations.literal: Annals of Taizong
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Emperor Taizong

translations.literal: Jian — mountain pronunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Jian: pronounced with the shan initial.

translations.literal: Where Husun Xi dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The dwelling place of the Husun Xi.

translations.literal: Mince — a ritual name.
translations.idiomatic: Mince: the name of a ritual.

translations.literal: Piling firewood to make an altar, receiving jade tablets from the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Firewood was piled to form an altar, and the emperor received jade memorials from his ministers.

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, firewood was burned to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended, a fire was lit to sacrifice to Heaven.

translations.literal: Instituted by Khan Zuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Established by Khan Zuwu.

sentences.zh: 遙輦氏九帳 遙輦九可汗宮分。

translations.literal: Nine Tents of the Yaolian Clan — the palace divisions of the nine Yaolian khans.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Tents of the Yaolian Clan: the palace households of the nine Yaolian khans.

sentences.zh: 北克、南克 掌軍官名，猶漢南北軍之職。

translations.literal: Northern Ke, Southern Ke — army-commanding office names, like the Han duties of the Northern and Southern Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Ke and Southern Ke: military command titles, analogous to the Han Northern and Southern Armies.

sentences.zh: 祭 鹿神 遼俗好射 鹿，每出獵，必祭其神以祈多獲。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to the Deer Spirit — Liao custom favored hunting deer; every time they went hunting, they necessarily sacrificed to its spirit to pray for abundant catch.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Deer Spirit: the Khitan loved deer hunting and always sacrificed to the deer god before a hunt, praying for a plentiful catch.

sentences.zh: 林牙 掌文翰官，時稱為學士。

translations.literal: Linya — an office managing documents; at the time called Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Linya: an official in charge of documents, commonly called an Academician.

translations.literal: Those established at the Pasturage Offices only managed ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: Those attached to the Pasturage Offices handled records only.

sentences.zh: 瑟瑟禮 祈雨射柳之儀，遙輦蘇可汗制。

translations.literal: Sese Rite — the ceremony of praying for rain and shooting willow branches; instituted by Yaolian Khan Su.
translations.idiomatic: Sese Rite: a rain-prayer ceremony involving willow-shooting, established by Yaolian Khan Su.

sentences.zh: 再生禮 國俗，每十二年一次，行始生之禮，名曰再生。

translations.literal: Rebirth Rite — a state custom, once every twelve years performing the rite of initial birth, called Rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: Rebirth Rite: a national custom performed every twelve years, a ceremony of symbolic rebirth called Rebirth.

sentences.zh: 惟帝與太后、太子及夷離得行之。

translations.literal: Only the emperor, empress dowager, crown prince, and yilij were permitted to perform it.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor, empress dowager, crown prince, and yilij could perform the rite.

translations.literal: Also called Covering Birth.
translations.idiomatic: It was also known as Covering Birth.

sentences.zh: 神速姑 宗室人名，能知蛇語。

translations.literal: Shensu Gu — an imperial clan personal name, able to understand snake speech.
translations.idiomatic: Shensu Gu: a member of the imperial clan who could interpret snake language.

translations.literal: Puge Jiang — the lower character uses the nai ding cut.
translations.idiomatic: Puge Jiang: the second character is pronounced with the nai initial and ding final.

translations.literal: A princess's name.
translations.idiomatic: The name of a princess.

sentences.zh: 三克 統軍官，猶雲三帥也。

translations.literal: San Ke — army-commanding official, like saying Three Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: San Ke: a military commander, equivalent to Three Commanders.

sentences.zh: 詳穩 諸官府監治長官。

translations.literal: Xiangwen — supervising chief of the various government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwen: the chief supervisory official of government offices.

sentences.zh: 梯裏已 諸部下官也，後升司徒。

translations.literal: Tiliyi — an official under the various divisions; later promoted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Tiliyi: a subordinate official; later elevated to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 達剌幹 縣官也，後升副使。

translations.literal: Dala Gan — a county official; later promoted to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dala Gan: a county-level official, later promoted to Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 麻都不 縣官之佐也，後升為令。

translations.literal: Mabudu — assistant to the county official; later promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Mabudu: deputy county official, later promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 馬步 未詳何官，以達剌幹升為之。

translations.literal: Mabu — office unclear; promoted from dala gan.
translations.idiomatic: Mabu: an office of uncertain function, attained by promotion from dala gan.

translations.literal: Yashu — an office name.
translations.idiomatic: Yashu: an official title.

translations.literal: Suspected to be yashu, a shilie office.
translations.idiomatic: Possibly yashu, an office of the shilie.

sentences.zh: 世燭 遙輦帳侍中之官。

translations.literal: Shizhu — an office of attendant-in-waiting in the Yaolian tent.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu: an attendant-in-waiting of the Yaolian tent.

sentences.zh: 敞史 官府之佐吏也。

translations.literal: Changshi — assistant clerk of a government office.
translations.idiomatic: Changshi: a deputy clerk in a government office.

sentences.zh: 思奴古 官與敞史相近。

translations.literal: Sinugu — an office close to changshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sinugu: an office similar to changshi.

sentences.zh: 徒睹古 邊徼外小國。

translations.literal: Tudugu — a small state beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Tudugu: a small state beyond the border.

translations.literal: Annals of Shizong and Muzong
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Emperors Shizong and Muzong

translations.literal: Feilong Shi — an office managing horses, also serving as vanguard escort.
translations.idiomatic: Feilong Shi: an official in charge of horses, also serving as a vanguard escort.

sentences.zh: 橫帳 德祖族屬號三父房，稱橫帳，宗室之尤貴者。

translations.literal: Hengzhang — Dezu's clansmen were called the Three Father Houses, termed Hengzhang — the most noble of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhang: Dezu's clansmen formed the Three Father Houses, called Hengzhang — the most exalted branch of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 著帳 凡世官之家及諸色人，因事籍沒者為著帳戶，官有著帳郎君。

translations.literal: Zhuzhang — all hereditary official families and various persons whose households were confiscated by registry became zhuzhang households; there were zhuzhang young lords.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuzhang: hereditary official families and others whose property was confiscated became registered zhuzhang households, served by zhuzhang attendants.

sentences.zh: 杓 印 杓 ，鷙鳥總稱，以為印紐，取疾速之義。

translations.literal: Shao Seal — shao is the general term for fierce birds; used as the seal knob, taking the meaning of swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Seal: shao denotes fierce birds of prey; used as the seal knob to signify speed.

sentences.zh: 凡調發軍馬則用之，與金魚符、銀牌略同。

translations.literal: Whenever armies and horses were mobilized it was used, roughly like the golden fish tally and silver plaque.
translations.idiomatic: It was used to mobilize troops, similar to the golden fish tally and silver plaque.

sentences.zh: 國舅帳克 官制有大國舅帳，此則本帳下掌兵之官。

translations.literal: Guozhang Ke — the official system had a Great State Uncle Tent; this was the military commander under that tent.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhang Ke: the bureaucracy included a Great State Uncle Tent; this was its military commander.

sentences.zh: 拜奧禮 凡納後，即族中選尊者一人當奧而坐，以主其禮，謂之奧姑。

translations.literal: Bai'ao Li — whenever a bride was received, the clan selected an elder to sit in the inner seat and preside over the rite, called the Ao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai'ao Li: when receiving a bride, the clan chose an elder to sit in the inner seat and preside — the Ao Gu.

sentences.zh: 送後者拜而致敬，故雲拜奧禮。

translations.literal: Those escorting the bride bowed in respect, hence called Bai'ao Li.
translations.idiomatic: Those escorting the bride bowed in homage, hence the name Bai'ao Li.

sentences.zh: 拜山禮 祀木葉山之儀。

translations.idiomatic: Baishan Li: the sacrificial rite at Mount Muye.

translations.idiomatic: Changwen: an official under the various tents.

translations.literal: Taizu recruited people to establish a stockade for exclusive mining and smelting, hence the name Xianhe Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu recruited settlers to establish a mining colony there, hence the name Sunken River Smeltery.

sentences.zh: 合蘇袞 女直別部名，又作曷蘇館。

translations.idiomatic: Hesugun: a Jurchen sub-tribe, also written Hesuguan.

translations.idiomatic: Hand-Clasp Rite: when a general defeated the enemy, the emperor clasped his hand in person;

translations.literal: if the general was in the field, someone was sent to perform the hand-clasp rite in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: if the general was still at the front, an envoy performed the rite on the emperor's behalf.

translations.literal: Four Victory Army — Liao divided Song surrenderers into two divisions: one called Four Victory Army, one called Return-to-Sagacity Army.
translations.idiomatic: Four Victory Army: surrendered Song troops were divided into two corps — the Four Victory Army and the Return-to-Sagacity Army.

translations.idiomatic: later renamed the Military Command Bureau.

translations.idiomatic: First-Fish Banquet: at the annual ice-fishing, when the first fish was caught, a feast was held — like the First-Goose Banquet.

translations.idiomatic: The army had a Zhua La Bureau;

translations.idiomatic: this office managed flags and drums.

sentences.zh: 九奚首 奚首，營帳名。

translations.idiomatic: Jie: a term for seasonal festival rites.

sentences.zh: 食 之次 大行殯出，群臣以 羊祭于路，名曰食 之次。

translations.literal: Jiu Xi Shou — xi shou is a camp tent name.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Xi Shou: xi shou is the name of a camp tent.

translations.literal: Shi Zhi Ci — when the late emperor's coffin was borne out, ministers sacrificed sheep on the road; called the Rite of Feeding at the Stop.
translations.idiomatic: Feeding at the Stop: when the emperor's coffin was carried out, ministers sacrificed sheep along the route — the Rite of Feeding at the Stop.

sentences.zh: 凡出征，以牝牡 各一祭之曰挻，詛敵也。

translations.literal: Yan Ji — the upper character uses the yu yan cut.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ji: the first character is pronounced with the yu initial and yan final.

sentences.zh: 勘箭 車駕遠歸，闔門使持雄箭，勘箭官持雌箭，比較相合，而後入宮。

translations.literal: Whenever setting out on campaign, one male and one female animal were sacrificed — called yan — to curse the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Before every campaign, a male and female animal were sacrificed in a rite called yan, to curse the enemy.

sentences.zh: 簷床 一人肩任曰簷，兩人以手共舁曰床。

translations.literal: Kan Jian — when the imperial carriage returned from afar, the Gate Commissioner held the male arrow and the Kan Jian official held the female arrow; comparing them for a match, only then could one enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Arrow Verification: when the emperor returned from a distant journey, the Gate Commissioner held the male arrow and the Verification Officer the female arrow; they had to match before entry to the palace.

sentences.zh: 攢隊 士卒攢簇，各為隊伍。

translations.literal: Yan Chuang — one person carrying on the shoulder is called yan; two people lifting together with the hands is called chuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Chuang: one person bearing a load on the shoulder is yan; two people lifting together is chuang.

sentences.zh: 方 、朵殿 凡禦宴，官卑，地坐殿中方墩之上；

translations.literal: Zuan Dui — soldiers clustered together, each forming a company.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan Dui: soldiers gathered in clusters, each forming a unit.

sentences.zh: 其不應升殿，則賜坐左右朵殿。

translations.literal: Fang Dun, Duo Dian — at imperial banquets, officials of low rank sat on the ground on square dun in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Square Dun and Side Halls: at imperial banquets, low-ranking officials sat on square dun in the hall;

translations.literal: those not permitted to ascend the hall were granted seats in the left and right duo halls.
translations.idiomatic: those not entitled to enter the hall were seated in the side halls to left and right.

sentences.zh: 正旦日，上於俼間擲米團，得只數為不利，則燒地拍鼠以禳之。

translations.literal: Dipai — a field mouse name.
translations.idiomatic: Dipai: a field mouse.

sentences.zh: 乃捏咿 正月朔旦也。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, the emperor threw rice balls in the tent; if the count came to an odd number it was unlucky, and field mice were burned to avert misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the emperor tossed rice balls in the tent; an odd count was inauspicious, and field mice were burned to dispel the ill omen.

sentences.zh: 挾裏坈 挾讀作狎，坈讀作頗。

translations.literal: Nainiyi — the first day of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Nainiyi: New Year's Day, the first day of the first month.

translations.literal: Xieli Kai — xie is read as xia, kai is read as po.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli Kai: xie is pronounced xia; kai is pronounced po.

sentences.zh: 六月十八日宴國舅族，亦曰挾裏坈。

translations.literal: The second day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The second day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 陶裏樺 上巳日，射兔之節名。

translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of the sixth month a banquet was held for the state-uncle clan — also called Xieli Kai.

translations.literal: Taoli Hua — on the third-day-of-the-third-month festival, the name of the rabbit-shooting festival.
translations.idiomatic: Taoli Hua: on the Double Third Festival, the name of the rabbit-shooting rite.

sentences.zh: 賽伊 奢 日辰之好也。

translations.literal: Tao Saiyi — Double Fifth Day.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Saiyi: the Double Fifth Festival.

translations.literal: Saiyi She — a favorable day and hour.
translations.idiomatic: Saiyi She: an auspicious day and hour.

translations.literal: Niehe Nai — dog's head.<Five>
translations.idiomatic: Niehe Nai: dog's head.<Note 5>

sentences.zh: 必裏遲離 重九日也。

translations.literal: Bilichi Li — Double Ninth Day.
translations.idiomatic: Bilichi Li: the Double Ninth Festival.

translations.literal: Daila — burning armor.
translations.idiomatic: Daila: burning armor.

translations.idiomatic: Chaowu Kai: the name of a battle.

translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Zhang: zhuo means to stand;

translations.idiomatic: zhang means a felt tent or yurt.

translations.idiomatic: Shilie Xingun: chief of the shilie office.

translations.idiomatic: Lingwen: an official title.

sentences.zh: 弭裏馬特本 官名，後升辛袞。

translations.literal: Mili Mateben — an office name; later promoted to xingun.
translations.idiomatic: Mili Mateben: an official title, later promoted to xingun.

sentences.zh: 麻普 即麻都不，縣官之副也，初名達剌幹。

translations.literal: Mapu — that is, mabudu, deputy to the county official; originally called dala gan.

sentences.zh: 知聖旨頭子事 掌誥命奏事官。

translations.literal: Zhi Sheng Zhi Touzi Shi — an office managing edicts and memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 提轄司 諸宮典兵官。

translations.literal: Tixia Si — military office of the various palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Tixia Si: the military administration office of the various palaces.

sentences.zh: 皮室昉軍制，有南、北、左、右皮室及黃皮室，皆掌精兵。

translations.literal: Pishi Fang — the military system had Southern, Northern, Left, Right, and Yellow Pishi, all commanding elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pishi Fang: the army included Southern, Northern, Left, Right, and Yellow Pishi units, all commanding elite forces.

translations.literal: Ting Fang — that is, the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ting Fang: equivalent to the Ministry of Works.

translations.idiomatic: Meili: an official title held by imperial relatives.

translations.idiomatic: Mogu: an official of the Wali Bureau.
